claims.text: A machine-learning-driven thermomechanical-processing approach can systematically tune HEA microstructure.
Tuning thermomechanical process parameters can significantly adjust the magnetocaloric response of non-equiatomic HEAs.
The as-cast, non-equiatomic HEA baseline is suitable for magnetocaloric applications.
Machine-learning-based high-throughput optimization can prescribe annealing, cooling, and forming schedules for HEAs.
Annealing temperatures from 800 to 1200 K are an appropriate optimization range.
Cooling rates from 1 to 50 K/s are an appropriate optimization range.
Cold working up to 50% before heat treatment is an appropriate optimization range.
The proposed processing variations will alter phase fractions in the non-equiatomic HEA.
The proposed processing variations will alter magnetic-domain structure, short-range ordering, and morphology.
Data-driven process selection can identify correlations among local microstructural evolution, magnetic transition temperature, and magnetocaloric performance.
Those processing–structure–property correlations can be used to enhance magnetic entropy change near an operating temperature.
Machine-learning-optimized processing will enhance magnetic hysteresis relative to conventional baseline treatments.
Machine-learning-optimized processing will improve magnetocaloric performance by approximately 10–20% relative to conventional baseline treatments.
The method is effective only for non-equiatomic alloys that remain single-phase or fine-scale multiphase.
Insufficiently comprehensive input data can limit the accuracy of the optimization model.
Extrapolation to untested compositions or processing regimes requires additional validation.
